skill.name: research
skill.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
skill.summary: Research technical questions with primary sources and save cited findings as a Markdown file.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The skill contains only prompt instructions in SKILL.md and no executable code. Static analysis produced no findings, and manual review found no prompt-injection text or malicious intent. It asks the assistant to save a Markdown research note, which is expected behavior for this skill.

content.value_statement: Technical research often loses citations or mixes secondary summaries with source facts. This skill directs Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to verify claims against primary sources and save a Markdown brief.
actual_capabilities: Directs the assistant to delegate research to a background agent.
Prioritizes official docs, source code, specs, and first-party APIs.
Requires each finding to cite the source that supports it.
Captures findings in a single Markdown file.
Saves research notes using existing repository conventions when available.
limitations: It depends on the host assistant having access to relevant sources and tools.
It produces research notes, not final business or legal decisions.
It may need user guidance when the repository has no note location convention.
It does not guarantee that sources remain unchanged after the report is written.

use_cases.title: Verify API Behavior
use_cases.description: Research how an API works using official docs, source code, or first-party references before implementation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Technical Decisions
use_cases.description: Collect source-backed facts for architecture notes, dependency choices, or migration planning.

use_cases.title: Improve Documentation Accuracy
use_cases.description: Gather cited evidence before updating docs, guides, or internal knowledge bases.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Research how this feature works using primary sources. Save a short Markdown report with citations for each claim.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Official Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for comparing documented behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the official documentation and source code for this API. Note any differences, cite each source, and save the findings as Markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Support a Technical Decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for planning a change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the tradeoffs for this migration using official docs, specs, and first-party examples. Produce a Markdown brief with evidence and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Knowledge
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for validating internal assumptions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this existing note against primary sources. Identify unsupported claims, source-backed corrections, and current references in a new Markdown research file.

output_examples.input: Research whether a framework supports streaming responses in its latest stable release.
output_examples.output: A Markdown note summarizing the supported streaming APIs, the official references used, version-specific caveats, and links for each claim.

output_examples.input: Find the source-backed differences between two package configuration options.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison brief with cited behavior, recommended follow-up checks, and the saved file location in the repository.

output_examples.input: Validate an internal architecture note before a migration discussion.
output_examples.output: A source-cited Markdown report listing confirmed statements, corrections, unknowns, and references to official documentation or source code.

best_practices: Ask a focused research question with clear scope and expected source types.
Prefer official docs, specifications, source code, and first-party API references.
Review the saved Markdown file before using it for decisions or publication.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad market summaries when primary technical evidence is required.
Do not treat secondary blog posts as final authority when official sources exist.
Do not use generated findings without checking citations for critical decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only skill that instructs the assistant to research and write Markdown.

faq.question: Will it browse the web automatically?
faq.answer: It depends on the tools available to Claude, Codex, or Claude Code in the current environment.

faq.question: What sources does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers official docs, source code, specifications, and first-party APIs over secondary summaries.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: It follows existing repository note conventions or chooses a sensible Markdown location.

faq.question: Can it help with documentation work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can collect cited evidence before you update guides, references, or internal notes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated advice?
faq.answer: No. It can collect primary sources, but expert review is required for regulated decisions.
